![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The comment states that `glamLevel: 0` is "out of range", and `stylePreset: ''` and `enforcedConstraints: []` are "invalid". However, looking at `promptCompilerMetadataSchema` in `validators.ts`, `glamLevel` is validated as `z.number()`, `stylePreset` as `z.string()`, and `enforcedConstraints` as `z.array(z.string())`. Therefore, these values are actually valid according to the schema, and only `imagePrompt` and `negativePrompt` (which violate `.min(1)`) cause the validation to fail.

To avoid confusion for future maintainers, please update the comment to accurately reflect which fields are actually invalid, or update the schema if stricter validation was intended for those metadata fields.

```suggestion
// Intentionally invalid: empty imagePrompt and negativePrompt (both violate min(1)).
// Used to prove validateCompiledPrompt() rejects malformed output.
```

In the sample scenario, `enforcedConstraints` is returned as the shared `constraints` array. If any test mutates `compiled.metadata.enforcedConstraints`, it will leak into subsequent `compile()` calls and can cause order-dependent/flaky tests. Return a fresh array (or clone) per call.

The comment above `compiledPromptFaultFixture` says it is invalid due to `glamLevel: 0`, empty `stylePreset`, and empty `enforcedConstraints`, but the current Zod schema allows those values (metadata.glamLevel is `number`, stylePreset has no `min(1)`, and enforcedConstraints has no minimum length). This is misleading; the fixture is invalid specifically because `imagePrompt` and `negativePrompt` are empty strings (min(1)).

The comment says the fault record is invalid due to an empty `images` array, but the schema is `images: z.array(generatedImageSchema)` with no minimum length, so an empty array is valid. The fixture is invalid because `id` and `createdAt` are empty (min(1)).
